# Revised cinematic viewpoints

Generated with built-in image_gen. This revision supersedes the fixed-camera requirements in layout_continuity_prompts.md. Frame 1 remains the canonical establishing shot; furniture identity and relative placement are preserved while the camera moves. Frames 2–5 use frame 1 and the archived previous_fixed_camera/03_discovering_vhs.png as references.

Use case: illustration-story / cinematic camera revision of an existing pixel-art game cutscene.
Deliver ONE full-bleed landscape image, 1672 x 941 pixels, approximately 16:9, no panels, borders, captions, UI or watermark.
Reference 1 is the canonical house establishing shot. Reference 2 is a reference for the living-room floor plan, furniture identity and character ONLY. IMPORTANT: invent a NEW CAMERA VIEW of this same physical set, do NOT copy reference 2's camera composition. The user specifically rejects four identical wide side views and the oversized wooden pillar on the left.
Set continuity: same Victorian house, faded small floral wallpaper above dark wooden wainscoting, dark parquet; one worn brown patterned wingback armchair with lace cloth on its back in the left portion of living room, one low rectangular dark wood coffee table in front of chair, one continuous rectangular burgundy/navy patterned rug beneath table, one modest bulky square CRT on low dark wooden stand across room to right, black front-loading VCR directly below CRT, tall dark shelving full of VHS tapes immediately behind TV. Same small portraits and one landscape picture on walls as reference 2, same ceramic pots on shelf. Foyer is outside living-room entrance; staircase is immediately alongside entrance, as in reference 1. No windows or curtains in the living room. Objects retain their physical positions while their screen positions/foreshortening naturally change with camera viewpoint.
Architectural correction: the oversized left foreground wooden column in reference 2 MUST NOT appear in the output. No freestanding columns, no pillars, no oversized posts or foreground wooden strips obstructing view. For interior shots the camera is fully inside living room and the doorway is outside the frame; normal uninterrupted wall surfaces and floor replace that obstruction. If entrance appears in frame 2 it is a normal wall-attached doorway, not a freestanding pillar.
Character continuity: one small eight-year-old boy in lime-green ogre-ear HOOD, cream shirt, brown vest, brown trousers/boots, orange jack-o-lantern candy BUCKET with handle and small orange flashlight; match face, cartoon proportions and costume in reference images, not adult ogre. One real child only. VHS tape is full-size black videocassette with cream label reading exactly "DO NOT PLAY". Keep lettering readable when label faces camera. No audio cassette.
Style: matching richly textured crisp pixel art, visible stepped edges and deliberate pixel clusters, dark outlines; amber hallway light contrasting with cyan CRT light, atmospheric but readable. Maintain mood and character design. No photorealism, no smooth 3D rendering, no gore, no extra furniture or objects.

## Frame 2

FRAME 2: REAR VIEW, shoulder-height medium-wide shot taken DIRECTLY BEHIND the boy in the foyer, looking over his back into the dim cyan television-lit living room. This is a new viewpoint rotated toward the living-room opening relative to reference 1. Boy stands centrally in foreground with his back squarely toward camera; show rear of green hood and its two ogre ears, back of brown vest, legs and boots. NO FACE VISIBLE, not a profile. His head tilts slightly with curiosity toward the lit room ahead. Candy bucket hangs from left hand, small flashlight in right, aimed forward/down. Boy occupies about 45 percent of image height. In front of him a normal wide doorway attached to the wall opens into living room: chair left beyond threshold, low table further inside, TV glowing toward upper-right deeper in room and shelf behind it. Near left wall show only a cropped section of the staircase adjacent to opening, consistent with reference 1; warm light from entrance is BEHIND camera. Compose warm-lit back silhouette framed by cold blue room. Do not show the original wide foyer layout or side-on character. No floating or freestanding pillar.

## Frame 3

FRAME 3: INTIMATE OVER-THE-SHOULDER DISCOVERY shot, camera now INSIDE living room, above and just behind boy's RIGHT shoulder, tilted downward about 30 degrees onto the coffee table. Completely different lens height and framing from reference 2. Back/right side of his green hood and shoulder occupy near left foreground, enough cheek profile to read curious expression, his orange flashlight illuminates the cassette. The low wooden coffee table dominates middle/lower image in foreshortened perspective; the SINGLE black VHS lies FLAT on the table, cream top label "DO NOT PLAY" facing camera and clearly legible. One empty sleeve beside it. Worn wingback chair with lace is visible beyond table at upper-left, and modest glowing CRT/stand and shelf are partially visible in upper-right background at their physically correct positions. A portion of the intact rectangular rug and straight border shows around table. This is a closer composition about the discovered tape, not a full-room establishing shot. The door, staircase and ALL wooden pillars/posts are OUTSIDE THE FRAME. No large foreground vertical architectural element. The room is continuous and unobstructed.

## Frame 4

FRAME 4: TIGHT SIDE THREE-QUARTER CLOSE-UP at VCR HEIGHT, camera inside room immediately beside the TV cabinet looking diagonally across the crouching boy's hands. Boy's face and green ogre-ear hood on left, his two hands and a realistically scaled VHS at center, VCR front face on right. Show the tape HALFWAY inserted horizontally into the VCR loading slot, with "DO NOT PLAY" label visible on its protruding edge. Both hands are clearly pushing one tape in, not holding two tapes. Upper-right edge contains a cropped portion of the same CRT glowing cyan above VCR; the TV may be cropped because this is an intimate close shot. Same low dark stand and same VHS shelving visible behind it. Lower edge may include orange bucket and flashlight on floor. Chair/table are far behind camera or at most tiny peripheral glimpses; do NOT squeeze the entire room into this close-up. Strong cyan rim light on face/hands, warm light from doorway off-camera. No doorway, stairs, column or pillar anywhere in this shot. Correct fingers, kid proportions, recognizable equipment. This should feel like a film insert of the decisive action.

## Frame 5

FRAME 5: DRAMATIC LOW-ANGLE WIDE shot from FLOOR LEVEL beside the coffee table, looking diagonally upward toward the existing TV and boy. The camera is fully inside living room, different from the high discovery shot and close-up insertion shot. Near corner and leg of same coffee table enter LOWER LEFT foreground with strong perspective, a sliver of worn chair farther left behind it; those are furniture, NOT tall columns. Right background contains SAME modest CRT on same low stand with VCR below and tape shelf behind. Do NOT grow or replace television. Boy floats diagonally upward from left toward TV at right, both arms reaching screen, face frightened, knees/feet trailing left, his fingertips dissolving into cyan pixel static where they meet glowing curved glass. Cyan-white static vortex emerges from screen with streaming dust and luminous pixel fragments. Orange jack-o-lantern candy BUCKET and small orange flashlight tumble through lower middle with a few wrapped candies, flashlight still lit. Tape already inside VCR, only empty sleeve stays on coffee table. Rug remains one rectangular rug with straight unbroken borders across floor beneath flight. Strong cinematic depth and foreshortening, mildly tilted composition allowed, maintain coherent furniture geometry. NO pillar, column, doorway post, window or curtains. No added furnishings. Not the reference's flat eye-level side view.
